 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** FTP** stands for** File Transfer Protocol**.
 
• It's a standard network protocol used for the transfer of computer files between a client and server on a computer network.
 
• FTP is built on a client-server model architecture using separate control and data connections between the client and the server.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are many protocols used in computer networking, each serving different functions and purposes. Some of the most commonly used protocols are:
 
 
• **Internet Protocol (IP):** It's primarily used to route packets of data from the source to the destination based on their IP addresses.
 
• **Transmission Control Protocol (TCP): **Works with IP to ensure that packets are reliably delivered. It manages error checking and retransmission of lost packets.
 
• **User Datagram Protocol (UDP): **A simpler, faster alternative to TCP that doesn't provide error checking or packet sequencing.
 
• **Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP):** The protocol used for transferring web pages and other content over the internet.
 
• **Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS): **A secure version of HTTP that provides encrypted communication and secure identification of network servers.
 
• **File Transfer Protocol (FTP):** A protocol for transferring files between systems.
 
• **Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP): **Used for sending email messages between servers.
 
• **Post Office Protocol 3 (POP3) **and **Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP)**: These are used to retrieve emails from a server.
 
• **Domain Name System (DNS): **Translates domain names into IP addresses.
 
• **Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP):** Used for managing and monitoring network devices.
 
• **Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP):** Assigns IP addresses to devices on a network.
 
• **Network Time Protocol (NTP): **Used to synchronize the clocks of computers over a network.
 
• **Secure Shell (SSH):** Allows for secure remote login from one computer to another.
 
• **Telnet**: An older protocol used for remote login. It's less secure than SSH.
 
• **Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP):** Mainly used by network devices to send error messages.
 
• **Address Resolution Protocol (ARP): **Resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses.
 
• **Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP): **Used by network devices for advertising their identities, capabilities, and neighbors on a local network.
